description: I'm passionate about space exploration, biotechnology, and the role of AI in solving real-world challenges. I'm  interested in understanding how the human body adapts to extreme environments and how technology can help protect human health beyond Earth.For this hackathon,I want to develop ORIGIN,an AI-powered astronaut health-monitoring platform that uses biological data,personalized health tracking,and predictive analytics to detect unusual physiological changes during space missions.
summary: Long-duration spaceflights expose astronauts to severe hazards—including space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity fields, and hostile closed environments—which can lead to physical and mental health risks like bone loss, cardiovascular deconditioning, and behavioral strain. To address this, we built ORIGIN, an interactive health monitoring software and gamified visual tool designed for astronauts to easily track health indicators (such as blood pressure, heart rate, fasting glucose, body temperature, sleep hours, mood, exercise, and radiation dose) and evaluate their status. The tool features color-coded alerts, dynamic trend charts, interactive body maps, and actionable guidance aligned with NASA's Human Research Program and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) research.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

  • What it does: ORIGIN is an interactive, gamified space health monitoring software designed for astronauts on long-duration missions. It enables crew members to log daily vital signs and qualitative metrics (such as blood pressure, heart rate, fasting glucose, body temperature, sleep hours, mood, exercise, and radiation exposure) to independently evaluate and act on their health status.
  • How it works:
    • Daily Quests: Astronauts complete daily check-ins using intuitive sliders and buttons.
    • Automated Assessment & Color Coding: The application instantly evaluates inputs against NASA-backed physiological thresholds and color-codes results (Green for OK, Yellow for Watch, Red for Alert) using a persistence model that tracks multi-day trends rather than noisy single-point readings.
    • Interactive Body Map: Users can tap an interactive 2D body map or avatar (Nova) to inspect specific systems (brain, eyes, heart, metabolism, immune system, muscles, bones, and radiation ring) to learn how space hazards affect them and what countermeasures to deploy.
    • Flight Surgeon Reporting: The app aggregates data into a structured medical report that can be copied, downloaded as a text file, or exported as CSV data.
    • 2. What benefits does it have?
    • Empowers Crew Autonomy: Gives astronauts the tools to spot health drift early on long missions where communication with Earth has significant time delays.
    • Actionable Guidance: Moves beyond raw numbers by providing immediate, plain-language instructions, countermeasures, and clear thresholds on when to contact flight surgeons.
    • Offline & Lightweight Reliability: Built as an offline-first tool that runs locally in the browser with no external installation required, ensuring mission-critical reliability even with limited connectivity.
    • What is the intended impact of the project?
    • Preventing Long-Term Health Degradation: Mitigates the severe risks mapped by NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP)—such as bone mineral density loss, cardiovascular deconditioning, radiation risks, and behavioral health strain during deep space exploration (e.g., Artemis missions or future Mars transit).
    • Enhancing Mission Safety: Reduces cognitive load and improves behavioral health tracking through consistent daily routines and gamified engagement.
    • What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?
    • Coding Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript for clean, responsive frontend logic.
    • Architecture & Software: Client-side local storage (localStorage) for secure, private on-device data retention, custom SVG graphics for the animated astronaut mascot (Nova) and body map, and dynamic charting logic.
    • Data Sources & References: Frameworks and parameters aligned with NASA Human Research Program (HRP) hazard/risk documentation and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) radiation monitoring research.
    • 5. How is your project creative?
    • Gamification in Space Health: Instead of a dry, clinical medical log, ORIGIN introduces Nova the astronaut mascot, who reacts emotionally and visually to the astronaut's health status.
    • Engagement & Progression: Users earn experience points (XP), unlock spacesuit color customizations, level up through ranks (from Cadet to Legend), maintain daily streaks, and earn achievement badges (such as Rested or Strong). This turns critical mission health compliance into an engaging daily habit.
    • 6. What factors did your team consider?
    • Spaceflight Constraints & Hazards: Explicitly accounted for NASA’s five hazards of human spaceflight (space radiation, isolation & confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, and hostile closed environments) and adapted the interface for different environments like the ISS, transit spacecraft, lunar bases, and Mars rovers.
    • False Alarms & Data Noise: Designed the alert logic to rely on multi-day persistence (e.g., 3-day trends) and multi-indicator strain patterns to avoid triggering false alarms from single noisy readings.
    • Accessibility & Usability: Incorporated a larger text accessibility mode, clear color-blind-friendly status chips, and intuitive controls designed for high-stress or low-gravity habitats
